scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three bearded men in long robes and sandals stand on a path amid golden wheat. One bends to pluck a grain head, one eats kernels from his palm, and one holds several stalks. Olive trees, hills, and a distant village lie beneath a blue sky in a warm watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The illustration imagines the hungry disciples plucking and eating grain in Matthew 12:1. Three men, wheat, their clothing, and the landscape are artistic choices; the verse does not specify their number or the grain species. Jesus remains outside the frame. The Sabbath setting comes from the source text and is not visually marked.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four robed men stand on a stone-lined path beside golden grain. At left, one man extends an open hand toward someone beyond the frame while his companion folds his arms. At right, two men hold grain heads and kernels. Olive branches, wildflowers and distant hills surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The two men at left represent Pharisees objecting to Jesus about His disciples, represented at right. Jesus remains outside the frame. The grainfield, grain in their hands, gestures and landscape are imaginative setting details; this verse itself records the Sabbath accusation without describing the disciples' activity or Jesus' reply.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three bearded travelers in cream, russet, green and ochre robes rest beneath an olive tree. The central man extends an open hand above an empty leather bag and earthenware bowl. Rocky hills and a distant village lie behind them in warm sunlight.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined pause represents David and his hungry companions, whom Jesus recalls in His question. The empty bag and bowl make their hunger visible; the resting place, clothing and number of companions are artistic choices, not details stated in this verse. Jesus remains out of view, and the bread episode is not shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a robed traveler breaking a round loaf beside a cloth-covered wooden table with bread on a golden tray. An ivory-robed priest stands nearby while two men eat bread beneath a woven doorway curtain. Hills and olive trees lie beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The sacred loaves and priest evoke the bread of the Presence, reserved for priests, while the travelers eating recall the event described in the verse. The sanctuary doorway, clothing, tray and two visible companions are imaginative choices; the verse does not specify their appearance or number.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three bearded men in ivory robes and linen head coverings serve in a sunlit stone temple courtyard. One lays wood on a burning horned bronze altar; the others carry firewood and a bronze bowl. A rolled scroll rests on a foreground stone ledge.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative courtyard shows priests tending an altar, carrying wood and holding a service bowl. Their willing labor pictures the Sabbath service Jesus cites; their calm expressions suggest guiltlessness without denying His word 'profane.' The rolled scroll alludes to His appeal to the Law. The verse does not specify these particular tasks, people or architecture. Jesus is outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed listeners, two bearded men and a woman in a blue mantle, look attentively toward the upper right beneath an olive tree. Sunlight warms their cream garments, limestone terrace and small purple flowers. Across the valley stands a pale stone temple complex with golden details under a soft blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The distant temple and nearby listeners imaginatively juxtapose the temple's honored grandeur with Jesus' declaration that something greater is here. The listeners attend to Him beyond the frame; He is not pictured. The terrace overlooking the temple is an artistic setting, not a location stated by this verse. Warm sunlight conveys attentive wonder rather than a depicted supernatural event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A traveler in olive robes places bread into the cupped hands of a seated traveler in blue beside a golden grain field. A clay water jug and cut grain rest nearby; an altar with a small flame in its bowl stands behind them among olive trees and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: These imagined travelers are not a recorded incident from the verse. Sharing bread pictures mercy, while the background altar recalls the mention of sacrifice. The seated traveler's dignified treatment invites reflection on Jesus' rebuke against condemning the guiltless. Neither traveler represents Jesus.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two men and a woman in modest robes sit beneath an olive tree beside a stone wall, looking attentively toward the upper left. A basket, folded cloth and unused hoe rest nearby. Golden grain, village houses and blue hills fill the sunlit background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined Sabbath setting pairs an unused work tool and resting listeners with attentive faces turned toward a speaker outside the picture. Their listening suggests recognition of the Son of Man's authority over the Sabbath. The verse states that authority; it does not describe these people, objects or this gathering. Jesus is kept outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a sunlit stone synagogue doorway beneath olive branches. A worn path leads across the threshold to a wooden stand with a rolled scroll. Two robed men sit on stone benches inside; village buildings and hills appear to the left.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The path and open synagogue doorway imagine the destination of Jesus' movement in Matthew 12:9 while keeping Him outside the visible scene. The stone building, olive tree, scroll and two seated worshippers are illustrative setting details that the verse does not specify. The image does not depict a healing or another subsequent event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a seated man in cream robes and a blue mantle, supporting the wrist of his thin, curled hand. Three robed men stand behind him; one gestures with an open palm toward the right. Sunlight enters the stone room through an opening overlooking distant hills and buildings.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The seated pose, stone room, clothing and gestures are imaginative staging for the man with a withered hand and the question asked to accuse Jesus. The standing men direct their attention beyond the frame, keeping Jesus unseen. The hand remains contracted: this illustrates the question about Sabbath healing, without depicting the later healing.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two hands in rolled linen sleeves support a cream-colored sheep as it rises from a rocky earthen pit, its front hooves reaching the rim. Olive trees, wildflowers, distant stone houses and sunlit hills surround the scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pictures the hypothetical rescue in Jesus' question, not a separately reported event. One sheep, the visible pit and the owner's supporting hands connect directly to taking hold and lifting it out. The peaceful hillside supplies an imagined setting; it does not visibly establish a Sabbath. Jesus remains outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, a younger man in ochre and blue offers a clay cup to a seated elder in olive and cream, resting a hand on his shoulder. A cream-colored sheep lies beside their bench beneath olive branches, with hills and village houses beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined act of offering water illustrates doing good and honoring human worth; the resting sheep recalls the verse's explicit comparison. This courtyard encounter is illustrative, not an event narrated in the verse or a depicted healing. Both men are unnamed neighbors, and Jesus is outside the composition.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a smiling bearded man in an olive tunic, cream striped mantle and cloth cap. He extends an open hand toward the left while looking at it; his other hand rests open near his waist. A stone bench and softly lit plaster and stone walls stand behind him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The extended, healthy hand pictures the restoration after the man obeys Jesus; his other open hand echoes the verse's comparison. Jesus remains outside the frame. The man's expression, clothing and simple stone interior are imaginative staging, not details specified by this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four bearded men in earth-colored robes and striped head coverings huddle beside an open stone doorway. One gestures while the others listen with furrowed brows. Sunlit paving, flowering plants, olive branches and distant hills surround them in warm watercolor.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The close, tense council imagines the Pharisees taking counsel against Jesus with the intention of destroying him. The four figures, their gestures and the stone courtyard are illustrative details, not details specified by the verse. Jesus remains outside the frame. No assault is shown: the verse describes their murderous planning.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A smiling crowd in long robes walks along a sunlit, olive-lined path. An elderly man holds his hands over his heart beside a woman in an ochre shawl; a mother rests her hand on a smiling boy. Stone village houses and blue hills rise behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined countryside procession pictures the many who followed Jesus and the gratitude of those He healed. Jesus remains beyond the bend, outside the frame; no visible person is the healer. The olive grove, village, individual people and their gestures are artistic details, not particulars supplied by the verse. The image suggests the outcome of His healing rather than reconstructing how each cure occurred.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three adults in earth-toned robes stand beneath an olive tree, looking attentively to the left. A woman holds a hand to her chest; the men keep their hands lowered. A stone wall, wildflowers, village houses and lavender hills fill the sunlit landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The quiet listeners imaginatively evoke those receiving Jesus' firm warning not to make Him known. Jesus stays outside the frame. Their number, clothing, gestures and hillside setting are artistic choices, not details stated in the verse; their attentive silence suggests the restraint His instruction requires.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An unmarked parchment scroll with wooden rollers rests on a sunlit stone ledge beside a reed pen and ink cup. An earthenware jug holds olive branches at left. A stone arch frames a flower-lined path through olive trees toward blue hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative still life uses the scroll to recall the word spoken through Isaiah. The sunlight and continuing path suggest fulfillment. Matthew 12:17 does not describe this setting or these objects; the unmarked parchment avoids inventing the prophecy's wording.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Five attentive listeners in blue, rust, ochre, sage and rose robes gather beneath an olive tree on a stone terrace. A mother rests her hands on a girl's shoulders. Clay vessels and flowers sit nearby; a sailboat, blue water and a distant hillside town fill the background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The varied listeners imagine the nations receiving the chosen servant's proclamation of justice. This harbor gathering is an imaginative setting, not a meeting reported in the verse. Jesus remains outside the frame; God's delight and the gift of His Spirit are affirmed by the text rather than depicted as visible beings.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A warm watercolor of a quiet stone village street. Grapevines shade a wooden doorway beside clay jars and a woven basket. A woman in a terracotta robe and cream head covering walks with a child in blue; olive trees, flowers and hillside houses fill the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined village street reflects the verse through its open space and absence of quarrelling or public outcry. The ordinary villagers are artistic additions. Jesus remains outside the picture; this is a meditation on His uncontentious manner, not a recorded incident or a claim that He never spoke publicly.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bruised green reed rises from shallow lake water beside a clay oil lamp on a stone ledge. Its wick glows faintly and sends up a thin curl of smoke. Golden dawn lights distant hills and a small stone house in a textured watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined lakeshore still life brings together the verse's bruised reed and smoldering flax wick, preserved rather than destroyed. It pictures Christ's gentleness without portraying Him. The dawn suggests hope; it does not literally depict His bringing justice to victory.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Six travelers in layered robes gather beneath an olive tree above a sunlit harbor. An elderly man rests his hands on a staff, a woman keeps a hand on a child's shoulder, and all look expectantly toward the upper right. Wildflowers line the stone path; sailboats and pale buildings lie beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering of Gentile travelers pictures the nations' promised hope in Jesus. Their shared gaze is directed beyond the right edge, leaving Him unseen. The harbor suggests different homelands; the verse does not describe this particular gathering, landscape, or clothing. Daylight is ordinary illumination, not a substitute for Him.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a seated, bearded man in an ochre tunic and blue mantle, looking upward with open eyes and parted lips. One hand touches his chest and the other opens outward. Two smiling men in olive and russet clothing accompany him beside warm stonework, olive branches and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene concentrates on the man's restored sight and speech after Jesus heals him. Jesus remains outside the frame. The courtyard, clothing and companions' gestures are imagined details, not specified by the verse. Demon possession is part of the verse's account, acknowledged in the explanation without inventing a visible spirit or ritual.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a crowd in a sunlit stone village. Seven foreground men and women in earth-colored robes show astonishment with open palms and lifted faces, while two men turn toward each other in questioning conversation. More villagers gather behind them beneath olive branches.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The crowd's amazed faces and the two neighbors' questioning exchange imaginatively express the verse's astonishment and question about the Son of David. Jesus remains outside the frame as the unseen focus. The courtyard, clothing, gestures and individual faces are artistic choices, not details specified by this verse; the picture does not turn their question into a coronation or formal declaration.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three bearded men in cream head coverings and earth-toned robes gather in a sunlit stone courtyard. One speaks with an outstretched hand while the others lean close, one resting his hand against his beard. Olive branches hang overhead beside a clay jar and stone bench.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The three speakers imaginatively represent the Pharisees making their accusation. Their tense discussion and outward gesture evoke speech about Jesus, who remains outside the frame. The courtyard and exact poses are reconstructed details. No demons appear: the verse records the charge that He works by Beelzebul, rather than a visible demonic event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Six adults in long robes dispute on opposite sides of a courtyard beside a limestone home with a collapsed central roof and scattered masonry. An olive tree, pottery and baskets frame the scene; a winding lane leads toward a partly ruined walled town beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The divided household beside its broken shared home and the ruined town imaginatively picture Jesus' warning that internal division brings desolation and prevents a kingdom, city or household from standing. The verse does not narrate this building collapse; the architecture is a visual analogy, and Jesus remains out of view.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor model of a walled stone city sits on a wooden table. A deep crack splits its earthen base and central arch, with loose blocks below and matching burgundy pennants above. Olive branches, pottery and sunlit hills surround it.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This is an imaginative teaching model, not a recorded event. Its single kingdom, broken through its own foundation, illustrates Jesus' conditional argument: if Satan casts out Satan, his kingdom is divided against itself and cannot stand. No figure represents Jesus, God or Satan.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four robed men, two older and two younger, consider one another beside a bronze balance holding equal pale stones in a sunlit stone courtyard. An olive tree arches overhead, with warm village buildings beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The courtyard gathering and balance are imaginative, not details stated in the verse. The equal stones suggest applying the same standard to Jesus and the accusers' own exorcists. The younger men evoke the sons or followers whose work challenges the accusation. Jesus is not depicted, and no exorcism is staged.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed adults look upward in a sunlit stone courtyard. A seated man opens his hands; two companions watch beside him. Olive branches, a clay jar and flowers surround them, and violet wisps curl beyond an open doorway.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The courtyard and people are imaginative, not details specified by the verse. The central man represents someone delivered, not Jesus; departing violet wisps suggest expelled demons. Ordinary daylight and grateful witnesses evoke God's reign already arriving. Jesus remains outside the frame; the Spirit is not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor stone-house interior shows a bearded man in a long olive tunic, tied to a wooden chair with his wrists bound in his lap. At the sunlit doorway, two hands lift a woven basket of clay vessels and folded cloth. An open wooden chest, jars, baskets, and a striped rug furnish the room.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined household illustrates Jesus' comparison, rather than a recorded burglary or a portrayal of Jesus. The restrained strong man and the goods being carried away express the sequence He states: first bind the strong man, then plunder his house. The setting and household details are artistic choices.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A green-robed worker binds a golden wheat sheaf beside a basket beneath an olive tree. A russet-robed worker walks away, dropping cut wheat onto a stony path, with fields, hills and pale village buildings beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined harvest contrasts a worker binding wheat with another walking away and letting cut stalks fall apart. It illustrates Jesus' opposition between gathering with Him and scattering, rather than documenting an event in the verse. Neither worker portrays Jesus.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four adults in olive, ochre, terracotta and blue robes listen intently toward the right beneath an olive tree in a sunlit stone courtyard. An elderly man and a cream-veiled woman sit together; a younger man holds a hand to his chest, and a blue-veiled woman stands behind. A clay jug, small flowers and distant hills complete the scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined group listens to Jesus outside the frame. Their sober attention reflects both the promise that sin and blasphemy will be forgiven and the grave exception: blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven. The courtyard and gestures are artistic inventions, not details given by this verse, and no listener is identified as guilty of that sin. The Spirit is not visually represented.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed adults sit beneath an olive tree in a sunlit stone courtyard. A woman cups her hands, a dark-haired man holds one hand near his lips and one palm open, and an older man rests folded arms over his knee. Flowers, an earthenware jug and distant hills surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering of listeners invites reflection on Jesus' solemn distinction between forgiveness for a word against the Son of Man and no forgiveness for speaking against the Holy Spirit, in this age or the coming age. The hand near the lips recalls the weight of speech; open and folded hands suggest differing responses. The verse does not describe this courtyard or these people, and the image assigns no one a verdict. Jesus and the Holy Spirit remain unseen. Human artwork review is pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor orchard with a leafy fig tree bearing plump purple and green fruit beside a hollow, decaying tree with curled leaves and shriveled dark figs. Fallen spoiled fruit lies near its roots; a sunlit path leads toward a stone wall and golden hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The two fig trees are an imaginative illustration of Jesus' comparison, not a recorded orchard visit. Sound fruit and spoiled fruit make each tree's condition visible. The verse does not specify a fruit species or setting.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A tipped terracotta jug pours muddy water into a stone channel. Three brown patterned vipers rest among rocks beside it. Olive branches, warm limestone walls, an arched doorway and flowers frame the sunlit courtyard.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The jug's dark contents pouring through its mouth imaginatively connect the heart's abundance to spoken words. Three vipers recall Jesus' sharp address, offspring of vipers. This is a symbolic still life, not a recorded courtyard event. No figure represents Jesus or God. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two open wooden chests sit on a sunlit stone ledge. One holds bread, grapes, figs and wheat spilling onto linen; the other holds thorn branches and spoiled fruit. Olive leaves shade the courtyard, and an arch frames distant hills and village houses.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative still life, not a recorded event: the two stores picture the good and evil treasure in the verse. Wholesome provisions and harmful thorns with spoiled fruit show how what comes forth corresponds to what is stored within. The objects are metaphors for moral character, not a claim that food or possessions determine goodness.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in cream clothing and a terracotta mantle sits with one hand against his mouth beside a blank parchment, three stones and a bronze balance. Flowers, olive branches, stone walls and distant hills surround the sunlit courtyard.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imagined listener reflects on his speech. The blank scroll, stones and balance are illustrative metaphors for giving account of every careless word on judgment day; the verse describes neither these objects nor this courtyard. The man is not Jesus, and no final-judgment event is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bronze balance holds a tied papyrus scroll in each pan on a stone table. A blank unrolled sheet and reed pen lie in front. Warm light and cool shadow cross the courtyard, with olive branches, a clay jug, a stone arch and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative still life is not an event described in the verse. The scrolls stand for a person's own words, and the scales recall the verdicts of justification and condemnation. Light and shadow emphasize those contrasting outcomes; they neither depict God nor imply that good words cancel evil words.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed men stand in a sunlit stone courtyard. One extends an open palm toward the left, while the others watch in that direction; the man at right holds a rolled scroll. Olive branches, clay jars and distant hills surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard scene visualizes the scribes and Pharisees asking their unseen Teacher for a sign. Their attentive faces and open hand express the request; Jesus remains outside the frame. The verse does not name the location, clothing or number of speakers, and no sign is shown as having occurred.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a long cream robe and rust-colored mantle stands on a sunlit rocky shore, head bowed and hand at his chest. A great fish's back and tail break the blue-green water beyond him; low headlands and a warm clouded sky fill the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative shore scene evokes Jonah, the prophet Jesus names as the sole sign. The shore and departing fish recall Jonah's story; they are not details narrated in Matthew 12:39 or a depiction of Jesus' audience. The humbled posture is an artistic choice. The verse rebukes an evil and adulterous generation for seeking a sign.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A whale-like sea creature swims beneath turquoise water beside a rocky coast. A round stone closes a tomb in the ochre cliff. An olive tree and shrubs grow above, while a pale moon hangs over a rose-and-gold twilight sea.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative coastal pairing compares the creature that held Jonah with a closed tomb recalling the Son of Man in the heart of the earth. Their shared shoreline is an artistic comparison, not a historical claim. Twilight suggests waiting without attempting to count or shorten the three days and three nights. Neither Jonah nor Jesus is shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor of a robed messenger seen from behind addressing men beneath an ochre city gate. A man in rough sackcloth kneels with his head bowed and a hand over his chest; an older man stands with lowered eyes and open palms. Other listeners gather around them, with sunlit city buildings beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative view of Jonah preaching in Nineveh illustrates the repentance Jesus cites as grounds for the Ninevites' future condemnation of His generation at the judgment. The architecture, faces and gestures are artistic choices. It does not depict the future judgment or Jesus, the One greater than Jonah whose presence makes the comparison so solemn.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A veiled queen in an ochre robe and teal mantle listens to a crowned king seated in a sunlit stone courtyard. Attendants stand behind her, and two laden camels follow a winding road through dry hills. Olive branches, flowering vines, pottery and woven cloth frame the watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined visit recalls the queen's journey to hear Solomon, the reason Jesus gives for her condemnation of this generation at judgment. The courtyard, clothing and caravan are artistic details. Jesus and the future judgment remain outside the picture; the verse declares that One greater than Solomon is here.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a barren rocky ravine, with cracked earth, thorn bushes, ochre cliffs and lavender hills beneath a pale sky. A small charcoal-gray wisp curls above the dry channel. No people are visible.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined waterless ravine illustrates the spirit's fruitless search for rest. The dark wisp is an artistic suggestion of the unclean spirit, not a claim about its visible form. Its departure from the person is outside the composition, and no later return is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An open wooden door reveals an empty stone-and-plaster room with a clean earthen floor. Sunlight falls beside a reed broom; clay jars, folded cloths, a basket, and a rolled mat are neatly arranged beneath timber rafters.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined ancient house visualizes the verse's house imagery rather than a documented building. The clean floor, broom, and arranged vessels show it swept and put in order; the vacant center emphasizes that it is unoccupied. The returning speaker remains unseen.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a sunlit stone house with an open wooden door and a dark violet interior. Pale gray and darker purple streams curl across the dusty lane into the doorway. A clay jar stands beside the steps; olive branches, village houses and blue hills surround the scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The house is an imaginative metaphor for the man, not a separate event asserted by the verse. The lighter wisp and gathering darker streams evoke the returning spirit and seven more wicked companions dwelling there, making his condition worse. The nearby village extends the image toward Jesus' warning about this evil generation. The shadows do not claim to show spirits' actual appearance.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A veiled woman and four robed men stand outside a sunlit stone house. One man extends an open hand toward a doorway, where seated listeners face farther into a shaded room. Olive branches frame the warm watercolor scene, and a clay jar rests by the threshold.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The waiting woman and men imaginatively represent Jesus' mother and brothers, and the shaded gathering recalls the crowds He was still addressing. Jesus remains out of view. The house, gestures, clothing and appearances are illustrative; the verse does not specify these details or explain why His family wished to speak.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bearded man inside an open wooden doorway gesturing toward a gray-haired woman in a blue shawl and two men standing in a sunlit stone courtyard, with olive branches, vines, clay jars and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The messenger's open hand connects his report to the mother and brothers standing outside. The doorway, clothing, expressions and two representative brothers are imaginative staging, not details specified by the verse. Jesus remains outside the picture.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Six robed adults sit closely inside a sunlit stone house, looking toward the upper left. A bearded man in a blue shawl rests a hand at his chin; an older woman wears a cream head covering. Olive branches and clay jars frame the warm watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The listening group imagines the pause after Jesus asks who His mother and brothers are. Jesus remains outside the frame; the central man represents the person He answers. The older woman and other adults evoke family without claiming to identify His relatives. The setting and expressions are artistic choices, not details specified by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Seven robed men sit closely on woven mats beside a sunlit stone doorway, looking toward an open hand entering from the lower left. Leafy branches shade the warm watercolor scene; clay vessels and distant houses complete the setting.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The open hand represents Jesus' gesture toward His disciples, while His face and body remain outside the image. Their close grouping evokes His words calling them His mother and brothers. The number, faces, clothing, house and light are imaginative setting details, not details specified by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Under an olive tree in a sunlit stone courtyard, a young woman touches an older woman's arm while a kneeling young man offers the older woman a clay cup. All wear modest robes, with soft hills visible beyond the courtyard wall.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative gathering uses caring fellowship among ordinary disciples to evoke the brother, sister and mother relationship Jesus names for whoever does His heavenly Father's will. The courtyard and offered water are artistic choices, not details narrated in this verse. Jesus and the heavenly Father are not depicted.
